reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that modern football reflects a broader systemic tension between tradition and innovation—mirroring political behavior. Strategic adherence duality (SAD) formalizes this as a balance between two competing forces: T (tradition) and R (radicalism). When these parameters diverge too far, strategic collapse ensues. The second primitive, Venerable vs. Merely Old (VMO), introduces a classification mechanism: D(V,O) = f(T,E) where E represents evolutionary pressure. If D falls below a threshold, outdated strategies dominate. Finally, Tactical Evolution Problem (TEP) captures how increasing complexity demands adaptive responses. These primitives form a triadic structure where SAD sets boundaries, VMO provides classification, and TEP drives change. Each operates within a shared mathematical space defined by information entropy and Bayesian updating. Failure modes include over-reliance on tradition (SAD imbalance), misclassifying old as venerable (VMO error), and failing to adapt (TEP collapse).
